result.title: Evaluating Type-1 Diabetes Digital Twins by Decision Quality
result.summary: A digital twin (DT) for type 1 diabetes (T1D) can predict how an individual's blood glucose will respond to different insulin treatments without actually trying them. For each treatment, downstream statistics of predicted glucose trajectories, such as glycemic risk, can be computed to guide clinical decisions. However, the quality of DTs is usually measured by the accuracy of their predicted glucose trajectories, which may not reflect the quality of the downstream treatment decisions they inform. In this work, we directly evaluate DTs by this decision quality on downstream treatment ranking, i.e., whether a DT predicts glucose trajectories that can be used to rank candidate treatments as the real patient would. We present an evaluation protocol over 30 virtual patients from the FDA-accepted UVA/Padova model, each simulated under 21 different basal-bolus treatments. For each patient, a DT is fitted under one treatment and then produces glucose trajectories for the remaining 20 treatments. Our results show that prediction accuracy and decision quality disagree. A baseline that models the average patient, never seeing the individual's glucose data, has the lowest prediction accuracy of all six methods (RMSE: 63.6 mg/dL) but ranks treatments with the second-highest mean Spearman (0.766), while a black-box neural network that predicts glucose nearly twice as accurately (RMSE: 32.9 mg/dL) ranks them no better than a random ordering of the 20 treatments (0.049 Spearman). Therefore, selecting a DT based on prediction accuracy alone can prefer one that recommends treatments at chance, and decision quality must be evaluated directly rather than assumed to follow from prediction accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文主张以「决策质量」而非血糖轨迹预测精度来评价 1 型糖尿病数字孪生，在 UVA/Padova 的 30 个虚拟病人与 21 种治疗方案上检验孪生模型能否像真实病人那样排序候选治疗。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预测精度与下游决策效用明显不一致」的结论可供核查 LVR 评价问题：潜状态对视觉细节的还原精度未必等于它对推理与答案的实际支撑，或需直接以决策或排序效用度量 latent 内容是否有用。
